title: Will physics be the next field to be turned upside down by AI? | New Scientist
description: AI has taken huge strides in computer programming and mathematics – physics could be next
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Antarctica’s ‘doomsday’ glacier will keep melting even if oceans cool | New Scientist
description: Computer models suggest that unrealistically cold oceans would be insufficient to stop Thwaites glacier retreating, although a neighbouring glacier might begin to grow
author: Alison George

title: Why a high school in Virginia is getting a quantum computer | New Scientist
description: Starting in January, students attending Skyview High School in Virginia will learn about the building blocks and principles underlying quantum computers by working with one directly
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Towering glacial ice cliffs may collapse in fits and starts | New Scientist
description: We still don't know for sure how the ice cliffs looming over the sea at the leading edge of some glaciers will behave as the climate warms, but satellite data offers some clues
author: Marissa Grunes

title: Google showcases way to fix quantum computer errors more efficiently | New Scientist
description: Error-proofing the most important operations performed on a quantum computer has so far required lots of resources, but a new experiment shows a more efficient way to make the devices reliable
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Probiotic cuts risk of respiratory infections in formula-fed babies | New Scientist
description: Babies who are formula fed are more prone to infections, but the addition of a probiotic supplement containing sugars from breast milk slashed the risk of such infants catching respiratory viruses
author: Carissa Wong
